notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise payments processor. Current LLM workloads run in a restricted VPC environment; they can use managed services but require private connectivity + strict audit trails.
- Primary pain: model rollouts causing latency regressions; they want automated rollback tied to production SLOs with strong guardrails (avoid flapping / cascading rollbacks).

Why now / context
- Referencing recent incident during a model version rollout (internal name: “routing-v2 canary”). They cited ~30–45 min to mitigate because rollback required manual validation + approvals.
- Quote from 2025-02-11 call: “If latency goes sideways, we need the system to self-correct faster than humans can get into the console.”

Product interest
- Redwood Dedicated for predictable capacity + isolation; paired with Redwood Private (VPC control plane) for compliance.
- Wants Console rollouts features: canary + automatic rollback + audit history view.

Technical + deployment constraints
- Deployment: VPC required (no public egress from their app workloads). PrivateLink acceptable.
- Regions: must support us-east-1 now; eu-west-1 required for a subset of EU cardholder workflows (data residency).
- Key management: KMS integration required; encryption-at-rest and in-transit baseline; asks about customer-managed keys for model logs.
- Logs/retention: request configurable retention controls for audit logs and rollout history (default retention needs to be stated).

SLO targets (used for rollback triggers)
- Latency SLO (chat): p95 end-to-end latency <= 900ms for typical prompts; they measure separately for streaming first-token and full completion.
  - First token: p95 <= 350ms (they consider this the user-visible metric).
- Error SLO: 5xx <= 0.3% over rolling 10 min; also asked for separate thresholds for 429/overload signals (they don’t want those to trigger rollback if caused by their own burst).
- Minimum traffic before rollback: they proposed >= 300 requests in the evaluation window (to avoid low-volume false positives).
- Comparison requirement: must be worse than baseline (previous stable) by a meaningful delta (they suggested +15% p95 latency OR +0.2% absolute 5xx).
- Cooldown: >= 30 minutes after rollback to prevent flapping.

Auto-rollback requirements (procurement focus)
- Must be available GA for their production start date; cannot be “best effort.”
- Controls:
  - Per-route / per-model / per-region thresholds.
  - Warm-up period: ignore first N minutes of a rollout (they suggested 8–10 min) while caches fill.
  - Safe behavior if monitoring is degraded: they prefer fail-open (do not rollback on missing/stale monitors) but want explicit “UNKNOWN” state + oncall notification.
  - Rate limiting: requested guardrails so one correlated monitoring event cannot trigger rollback across multiple tenants/regions simultaneously.
- Visibility:
  - Console shows current verdict (HEALTHY / BREACH / COOLDOWN / UNKNOWN), recent evaluation windows, and the exact monitor query used.
  - Rollback history w/ reason + “what traffic split changed” and link to runbook.
- Notifications:
  - Slack notification to their #ml-oncall channel + webhook option.
  - They asked about PagerDuty integration (not required for day-1, but want an API/event stream).
- Compliance/audit:
  - Audit events must include actor = system, policy version, monitor ids, evaluated metrics, and executor action (traffic split revert) + idempotency key.

Open questions captured
- Clarify how error-rate is defined (HTTP 5xx only vs includes model timeouts). They currently count request timeouts as errors.
- Clarify if rollback decisioning can exclude incidents tagged as “upstream network” (they want to avoid rollback during broader infra incidents).
- Confirm if Dedicated tier SLOs differ from Hosted defaults; they want contractual SLOs aligned with what triggers rollback.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-01-23: Reliability deep dive (Fireflies ff-90113). Focus on SLO evaluation windows, flapping prevention, and audit log needs.
- 2025-02-03: Security intake started; requested Security FAQ + audit logging examples (Drive: Security_FAQ_Redwood_Inference_Private_VPC.pdf).
- 2025-02-11: Escalation sync post-incident (Fireflies ff-90144). Re-emphasized automatic rollback + “must be worse than baseline.”
- 2025-02-14: Referenced support escalation SUP-18421 (latency regression during rollout) as the motivating event.
- 2025-02-20: Procurement call: asked for contract language tying rollback automation to rollout controller / SLO monitors (not just “monitoring exists”).
- 2025-02-25: Sent draft addendum language; waiting on their legal redlines; engineering asked to confirm per-region threshold support (they referenced SUP-18490).

Next steps
- Ava Chen to send consolidated response on (1) fail-open semantics, (2) audit event examples, (3) per-region/per-tier policy support.
- Hannah Rivera to schedule technical working session with their SRE lead to map monitor identity: route/model/region/tier labels and confirm minimum-traffic guardrails.
